result: The authors successfully generated and characterized transgenic N. attenuata lines with silenced TPI production (irPI) and GLV production (irLOX2 and hemi-irLOX2). The irPI line had no detectable TPI activity and only 0.3% of WT PI transcript levels. The irLOX2 line had <10% of WT GLV levels, while hemi-irLOX2 had 20-40% of WT GLV levels. Other HIPVs like (E)-α-bergamotene were not affected, and jasmonate signaling remained intact.

result: Geocoris spp. predators consistently preferred to predate Manduca larvae and eggs from GLV-emitting or GLV-supplemented plants. Predation rates were 2-4 times higher on WT and irPI plants (43-60% for larvae, 34-39% for eggs) compared to GLV-deficient irLOX2 and hemi-irLOX2 plants (17-33% for larvae, 9-20% for eggs). result: In matched plant experiments, GLV-mediated predation increased plant fitness. In 2010 without Geocoris predation, genotypes showed no differences in Manduca mortality or reproduction. In 2011 with active predators, larval mortality on hemi-irLOX2 was half that on WT/irPI, and hemi-irLOX2 plants produced 40-50% fewer buds, flowers, and seed capsules than WT/irPI plants. The authors conclude that GLV emissions function as indirect defenses by doubling predation rates and plant reproduction.

result: The authors propose that HIPVs and PIs could be employed in integrated pest management strategies. Indirect defenses promise an effective first line of defense to which herbivores are unlikely to rapidly evolve resistance.
